en: Ice floats on liquid water because water uniquely expands and becomes less dense when it freezes into a solid.
When iron rusts, it chemically combines with oxygen in the air to actually gain mass and become heavier.
A mixture of cornstarch and water acts as a solid when you punch it but flows like a liquid when you pour it.
Diamonds and the graphite in your pencil are both made of the exact same pure carbon atoms arranged differently.
Even though we rarely see it on Earth, plasma is actually the most common state of matter in the entire universe.
Dry ice is solid carbon dioxide that skips the liquid phase entirely and sublimates directly into a cold gas.
The metal gallium melts at thirty degrees Celsius, meaning it will turn into a liquid pool just by holding the solid in your warm hand.
Bending a glow stick breaks an inner glass vial, mixing chemicals that release energy as visible light instead of heat.
Water molecules stick together so tightly at the surface that their strong surface tension can actually support the weight of a walking water strider insect.
Scientists remove almost all the liquid from a silica gel mixture to create aerogel, a solid material that is 99 percent air.
Liquid nitrogen is so extremely cold at minus 196 degrees Celsius that it instantly freezes a fresh flower completely solid.
Frying an egg is an irreversible chemical change because the heat permanently alters the protein molecules, meaning you can never turn it back into a raw egg.
